question: A woman sustains a perineal laceration during delivery that extends through the perineal skin, vaginal epithelium, and the perineal body muscles but does NOT involve the anal sphincter complex. How is this injury classified?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A first-degree tear involves only the perineal skin and vaginal mucosa — it does not involve the underlying perineal body muscles. This injury goes deeper, reaching the muscles.

Correct. A second-degree tear extends through the perineal skin, vaginal epithelium, AND the perineal body muscles (including bulbocavernosus and transverse perinei), but does not involve the anal sphincter complex. Repair typically requires suturing in layers.
Incorrect. A third-degree tear additionally involves the external anal sphincter (and possibly the internal anal sphincter). The injury described here spares the anal sphincter complex entirely.
Incorrect. A fourth-degree tear involves the perineum, the full anal sphincter complex (EAS + IAS), AND breaches the rectal mucosa. The injury described here involves none of the anal structures.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the obstetric perineal tear classification: 1st = skin/mucosa only; 2nd = skin + perineal body muscles; 3rd = + anal sphincter (EAS ± IAS); 4th = + rectal mucosa breach.
Well done. Second-degree tears are the most common tears requiring formal suture repair; they extend into the perineal body muscles but spare the anal sphincter.
